List the 5 most deadly cancers, and indicate the 5-year survival rate in brackets. In another, separate list, list 5 uncommon cancers, and give a rough indication (or specific numbers if possible) of how many cases of each there are per year in the United States.  Make sure no cancer appears in both lists. 

Order the deadliest cancers list from most to least deadly, and order the uncommon cancers list by cases per year (ascending). List the uncommon cancers first, and begin with a short paragraph about cancer survival rates in the US. Don't include pancreatic cancer in the deadliest cancers list (it's already accounted for in my presentation). Don't give the lists any headings or introductions but do give the response as a whole one.

arguments.content:
In the United States overall cancer 5-year survival has improved over decades; for all cancers combined the population-level 5-year relative survival is roughly 65–70% (varies by age, stage and cancer type). Survival varies widely by tumor type and stage — the lists below use (a) “uncommon” = low annual incidence in the US, and (b) “most deadly” = lowest typical 5‑year relative survival (pancreatic was excluded as requested).

- Adrenocortical carcinoma — ~300–400 cases per year in the US (very rare, ≈1 per million/year).
- Thymoma / thymic carcinoma — ~400–600 cases per year in the US.
- Primary central nervous system lymphoma — ~1,000–1,800 cases per year in the US (rare extranodal lymphoma of the brain/eye/CNS).
- Uveal (ocular) melanoma — ~2,000 cases per year in the US.
- Merkel cell carcinoma — ~2,500–3,500 cases per year in the US.

Glioblastoma (GBM) — 5‑year survival ~5–10% (very poor)
Small‑cell lung cancer — 5‑year survival ~7–10%
Mesothelioma — 5‑year survival ~10–12%
Esophageal cancer — 5‑year survival ~20–25%
Hepatocellular carcinoma (primary liver cancer) — 5‑year survival ~20–25%

Concise reasoning: “Uncommon” list ordered from fewest to most annual US cases (estimates rounded); “most deadly” list ordered from lowest to higher 5‑year relative survival (pancreatic omitted). Numbers and survival figures are approximate population-level estimates and vary by stage, patient factors and source year.
